description: Gather information about EC2 Classic Elastic Load Balancers in AWS.

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: List of ELB names to gather information about. Pass this option to gather information about a set of ELBs, otherwise, all ELBs are returned. Default: []

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
# Note: These examples do not set authentication details, see the AWS Guide for details.
# Output format tries to match amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb module input parameters

- name: Gather information about all ELBs
  amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb_info:
  register: elb_info

- ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "{{ item.dns_name }}"
  loop: "{{ elb_info.elbs }}"

- name: Gather information about a particular ELB
  amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb_info:
    names: frontend-prod-elb
  register: elb_info

- ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "{{ elb_info.elbs.0.dns_name }}"

- name: Gather information about a set of ELBs
  amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb_info:
    names:
      - frontend-prod-elb
      - backend-prod-elb
  register: elb_info

- ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "{{ item.dns_name }}"
  loop: "{{ elb_info.elbs }}"

return_values.name: elbs
return_values.description: A list of load balancers. Returned: always

return_values.name: attributes
return_values.description: Information about the load balancer attributes. Returned: always

return_values.name: access_log
return_values.description: Information on whether access logs are enabled or not. Returned: success Sample: {"enabled": false}

return_values.name: additional_attributes
return_values.description: Information about additional load balancer attributes. Returned: success Sample: [{"key": "elb.http.desyncmitigationmode", "value": "defensive"}]

return_values.name: connection_draining
return_values.description: Information on connection draining configuration of elastic load balancer. Returned: success Sample: {"enabled": true, "timeout": 300}

return_values.name: enabled
return_values.description: Whether connection draining is enabled. Returned: always

return_values.name: timeout
return_values.description: The maximum time, in seconds, to keep the existing connections open before deregistering the instances. Returned: always

return_values.name: connection_settings
return_values.description: Information on connection settings. Returned: success Sample: {"idle_timeout": 60}

return_values.name: cross_zone_load_balancing
return_values.description: Information on whether cross zone load balancing is enabled or not. Returned: success Sample: {"enabled": true}

return_values.name: availability_zones
return_values.description: The Availability Zones for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: ["us-west-2a"]

return_values.name: backend_server_descriptions
return_values.description: Information about your EC2 instances. Returned: always Sample: [{"instance_port": 8085, "policy_names": ["MyPolicy1"]}]

return_values.name: canonical_hosted_zone_name
return_values.description: The DNS name of the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: "test-123456789.us-west-2.elb.amazonaws.com"

return_values.name: canonical_hosted_zone_name_id
return_values.description: The ID of the Amazon Route 53 hosted zone for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: "Z1Z1ZZ5HABSF5"

return_values.name: created_time
return_values.description: The date and time the load balancer was created. Returned: always Sample: "2024-09-04T17:52:22.270000+00:00"

return_values.name: dns_name
return_values.description: The DNS name of the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: "test-123456789.us-west-2.elb.amazonaws.com"

return_values.name: health_check
return_values.description: Information about the health checks conducted on the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: {"healthy_threshold": 10, "interval": 5, "target": "HTTP:80/index.html", "timeout": 2, "unhealthy_threshold": 2}

return_values.name: healthy_threshold
return_values.description: The number of consecutive health checks successes required before moving the instance to the Healthy state. Returned: always

return_values.name: interval
return_values.description: The approximate interval, in seconds, between health checks of an individual instance. Returned: always

return_values.name: target
return_values.description: The instance being checked. The protocol is either TCP, HTTP, HTTPS, or SSL. The range of valid ports is one (1) through 65535. Returned: always

return_values.name: unhealthy_threshold
return_values.description: The number of consecutive health checks successes required before moving the instance to the Unhealthy state. Returned: always

return_values.name: instances
return_values.description: The IDs of the instances for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: [{"instance_id": "i-11d1f111ea111111b"}]

return_values.name: instances_inservice
return_values.description: Information about instances for load balancer in state “InService”. Returned: always Sample: ["i-11d1f111ea111111b"]

return_values.name: instances_inservice_count
return_values.description: Total number of instances for load balancer with state “InService”. Returned: always Sample: 1

return_values.name: instances_outofservice
return_values.description: Information about instances for load balancer in state “OutOfService”. Returned: always Sample: ["i-11d1f111ea111111b"]

return_values.name: instances_outofservice_count
return_values.description: Total number of instances for load balancer with state “OutOfService”. Returned: always Sample: 0

return_values.name: instances_unknownservice
return_values.description: Information about instances for load balancer in state “Unknown”. Returned: always Sample: ["i-11d1f111ea111111b"]

return_values.name: instances_unknownservice_count
return_values.description: Total number of instances for load balancer with state “Unknown”. Returned: always Sample: 1

return_values.name: listener_descriptions
return_values.description: Information about the listeners for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: [{"listener": {"instance_port": 80, "instance_protocol": "HTTP", "load_balancer_port": 80, "protocol": "HTTP"}, "policy_names": []}]

return_values.name: load_balancer_name
return_values.description: The name of the elastic load balancer. Returned: always Sample: "MyLoadBalancer"

return_values.name: policies
return_values.description: Information about the policies defined for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: {"app_cookie_stickiness_policies": [], "lb_cookie_stickiness_policies": [], "other_policies": []}

return_values.name: app_cookie_stickiness_policies
return_values.description: The stickiness policies created using CreateAppCookieStickinessPolicy. Returned: always

return_values.name: lb_cookie_stickiness_policies
return_values.description: The stickiness policies created using CreateLBCookieStickinessPolicy. Returned: always

return_values.name: other_policies
return_values.description: The policies other than the stickiness policies. Returned: always

return_values.name: scheme
return_values.description: The type of load balancer. Returned: always Sample: "internet-facing"

return_values.name: security_groups
return_values.description: The security groups for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: ["sg-111111af1111cb111"]

return_values.name: source_security_group
return_values.description: The security group for the load balancer, which are used as part of inbound rules for registered instances. Returned: always Sample: {"group_name": "default", "owner_alias": "721111111111"}

return_values.name: group_name
return_values.description: The name of the security group. Returned: always

return_values.name: owner_alias
return_values.description: The owner of the security group. Returned: always

return_values.name: subnets
return_values.description: The IDs of the subnets for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: ["subnet-111111af1111cb111"]

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: The tags associated with a load balancer. Returned: always Sample: {"Env": "Dev", "Owner": "Dev001"}

return_values.name: vpc_id
return_values.description: The ID of the VPC for the load balancer. Returned: always Sample: "vpc-0cc28c9e20d111111"
